findings.title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
findings.summary_md: Android Authority reported on Nov. 5, 2026 that GhostMap lets a specially crafted app trigger a persistent boot loop simply by being installed. The app needs no permissions, contains no executable code, and never has to be launched. The article notes Google knew about the flaw since August and closed it as not reproducible without shipping a fix.

findings.title: GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app
findings.summary_md: Bitdefender Labs disclosed GhostMap on Nov. 5, 2026, an Android denial-of-service flaw found after a banking dropper from the wild crashed its analysis emulators on Aug. 12, 2026. Two Android libraries interpret ZIP compression differently, letting a malformed APK bypass size checks and be mapped past its contents; reading the entry triggers SIGBUS. The flaw was reproduced on a Pixel 10 with Android 17 and the Aug. 5, 2026 patch and affects Android 10 and above; Google closed the August report as not reproducible with no patch.
